title: MiniMax-M1
hook: MiniMax-M1 is an open-weight reasoning model with a million-token context and 'lightning attention' — and a hybrid design that made full RL training cost about $0.5M.
key_points: Open-weight hybrid-attention reasoning model from MiniMax, June 2025.
456B-parameter MoE (45.9B active) with a native 1M-token context — 8× DeepSeek-R1.
Lightning attention scales test-time compute efficiently for long inputs and long thinking.
Trained with the CISPO RL algorithm; full RL run finished in ~3 weeks on 512 H800s.
content_html: MiniMax-M1 is an open-weight, large-scale hybrid-attention reasoning model released by MiniMax in mid-2025. Built on a 456-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts backbone (about 45.9 billion active per token), its headline feature is a native one-million-token context window — eight times that of DeepSeek-R1 — supported by an efficient "lightning attention" mechanism.
extra_html:
How it works

Standard attention costs grow quadratically with sequence length, which is what makes very long contexts and very long reasoning chains expensive. MiniMax-M1 mixes lightning attention with a Mixture-of-Experts design so that both the long inputs and the extended "thinking" needed for reasoning scale efficiently. Training used a new RL algorithm, CISPO, which clips importance-sampling weights rather than token updates; combined with the efficient architecture, the full reinforcement-learning run completed in roughly three weeks on 512 H800 GPUs at a reported rental cost around $535K — strikingly cheap for a frontier-style reasoning model.

Why it matters

M1 is two trends in one model: open-weight frontier reasoning, and architectural efficiency aimed squarely at the cost of long-context, long-thinking inference. The economics are the story — demonstrating that competitive RL-trained reasoning need not require a nine-figure budget pushes the open ecosystem forward.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute
related.hook: A new scaling axis: instead of a bigger model, let a model think longer at inference — often a better use of compute, and the principle behind o1 and R1.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.
